summary:
H.R. 9094, the "Florida Freeze Disaster Assistance Act of 2026," appropriates funds to the Secretary of Agriculture to provide block grants to States for agricultural losses resulting from specified freeze or cold weather conditions. Section 2 appropriates $3,500,000,000 out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, as an additional amount for the "Office of the Secretary" of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, to remain available until expended. 

The Secretary shall use these funds to provide assistance in the form of block grants to States to compensate for losses of revenue, quality, or production of crops (including crops prevented from planting), trees, bushes, and vines caused by a freeze or cold weather condition. The appropriation expressly includes compensation to producers for losses of multi-year crops. 

The bill imposes material geographic limitations and conditions precedent on the disbursement of funds. The assistance is available exclusively for losses occurring in counties that received a disaster designation for freeze and related cold weather conditions issued by the Secretary on March 4, 2026. Furthermore, funds are made available only upon the request of a State department of agriculture or another appropriate State agency as determined by the Secretary. 

The bill also establishes a reporting requirement, mandating that the Secretary submit a report to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations not later than 120 days after the date of enactment, and for each fiscal quarter thereafter until the appropriated amounts are expended, describing the implementation of the assistance provided under the Act. Finally, the appropriation is designated by Congress as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(A)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985.
